messages:
maria gonzalez: Quick thought — what if we stop using per-prefix leases as the canonical eviction/ownership primitive? Proposal: deterministic demarcation based on prefix hash + epoch manifest in the coord store. Fewer lease renew RPCs on hot prefixes, simpler serving fast-path. Thoughts?

sam nguyen: Interesting. My immediate worry is split-brain: how do we avoid two nodes both thinking they own the same prefix during topology churn? Leases gave clear liveness/ownership semantics.

maria gonzalez: Yeah, good call. The idea is to replace continuous leases with discrete "claims" that are CAS-writable into a prefix manifest. Each claim carries (prefix, epoch, node_id, seq). Serving is allowed only when local epoch == manifest epoch. On topology change we bump epoch, CAS new owner. That makes handover a single write instead of repeated heartbeats.

linh tran: So it's lease-free but still relies on a central manifest store for atomicity. Seems like a weaker but cheaper lease. Two questions: (1) read-after-write correctness for callers — how do we ensure readers don't observe stale state while the claim switch is propagating? (2) What about in-flight requests from the old owner?

maria gonzalez: For (1) we add a small soft-ttl on cached responses and include manifest_epoch/version in responses. Clients can attach the epoch they observed; origin can reject if mismatch. For (2) in-flight can include epoch token; if the new owner sees responses from old epoch it discards or revalidates. The invariants: only one epoch should be authoritative in the manifest.

rahul: Need instrumentation: track claim_nonce, manifest_epoch, contested_count, and time_to_claim. Also add an alert when contested_count > X or manifests flip frequently for a prefix.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canaries launched for kv-leasefree-proto on canary pool (pool-canary-3). Logs at https://ci.internal/reports/3756 — be aware of increased manifest ops during warmup.

sam nguyen: Edge cases: prefix split/merge. If we split a prefix and both halves try to claim, the manifest update needs to be atomic across the namespace. Suggest manifest supports multi-key CAS or we use a versioned prefix manifest and a single CAS against manifest_id -> manifest_blob.

linh tran: For merges we need to ensure sequence numbers are monotonic so evidence of stale claims is easy to reject. Also consider a short grace period where both old owner and new owner serve but with degraded throttling, to absorb client retries.

maria gonzalez: Implementation sketch: 
- manifest record: {prefix_range, epoch, owner_node, sequence, tombstone_ts?}
- claim flow: read manifest, compute new epoch = manifest.epoch + 1, attempt CAS(manifest_id, old_blob, new_blob).
- serve guard: only serve requests when local_epoch == manifest.epoch. Attach epoch header to responses.
- fallback: if CAS fails repeatedly, fall back to current lease-based path for that prefix for N minutes (migration window).

sam nguyen: That fallback is crucial. We shouldn't roll a migration that immediately weakens safety without a stopgap. Also need an operator command to force-rollover in emergencies.

rahul: Tests: chaos scenarios — crash owner during CAS, network partition between coord store and node, split/merge flapping. We'll need a deterministic test harness that can assert no dual-serve and bounded staleness. I'll prototype the harness.

linh tran: One more thought: GC of stale claims. If a node crashes and never clears its claim, we rely on epoch bumping, but manifest entries might accumulate tombstones. Keep a tombstone TTL and compaction job. Also ensure we never reuse the same epoch value for a prefix (monotonic counter).

maria gonzalez: Tradeoffs summary I put in my head: 
- Pros: fewer steady-state RPCs for hot prefixes, cheaper tail latency, simpler hot-path checks.
- Cons: more complexity in manifest CAS semantics, harder split/merge correctness surface, need more telemetry and deterministic tests.

sam nguyen: Work items: RFC with data model + invariants, migration plan (fallback window + operator commands), CAS implementation options (etcd/generic KVS vs. single manifest blob), and chaos tests. I'll take CAS options writeup.

rahul: I'll own the chaos harness and metrics change.

linh tran: I'll prototype epoch-tag propagation in the RPC layer and the soft-ttl behavior.

maria gonzalez: I'll draft the RFC today with diagrams and a minimal sequence diagram for split/merge. Aim to ship a canary within 2 sprints if everyone signs off.

sam nguyen: sgtm. Thanks.

rahul: :thumbsup:

maria gonzalez: quick note — include an explicit invariant in the RFC: "At any time t after manifest commit, there exists at most one node that will accept new write traffic for prefix P at epoch E". We'll need tests to assert that under failures.

linh tran: good invariant. I'll add a cheap unit test that simulates two nodes racing the CAS and asserts only one becomes authoritative.

maria gonzalez: thanks all — I'll ping when the draft is up.

sam nguyen: ty!
